passwordHelpText: Click the tab button to move between inputs. Shift+tab - moves back one input. An empty column means there is no limit for that position. You can also click on letters buttons.
morseHelpText: Morse code can be entered from any point during transmission. The search algorithm operates cyclically (looped search), so the match also includes fragments that move from end to beginning.
whosonfirstHelpText: Position map (display → read). Codes: P/L = left/right column, G/Ś/D = top/middle/bottom

common.noData: No data in this language file.

banner.title: COMPLETE
banner.desc: This module needs it now, but it is still “?” in the panel. Click below (saves globally):

simon.title: Simon Says
simon.help: Click the colors in the order they flashed on the bomb. The program maps them through the table (serial vowel + strikes) and shows what to press.
simon.needVowel: FIRST ENTER ABOVE WHETHER THE SERIAL HAS A VOWEL — the table is unknown without it.

wires.title: Wires
wires.help: Click the 5 color buttons in bomb order (top to bottom). Wires draw below, and the program recalculates which one to cut with every click. Set the last serial digit parity in the left panel.
wires.emptyState: Nothing clicked yet — click the first (top) wire.
wires.r3a: 3 wires: no red wires → cut the 2nd wire.
wires.r3b: 3 wires: last wire white → cut the last wire.
wires.r3c: 3 wires: more than 1 blue → cut the last blue wire.
wires.r3d: 3 wires: otherwise → cut the last wire.
wires.r4a: 4 wires: >1 red + odd serial → cut the last red wire.
wires.r4b: 4 wires: last yellow + no red → cut the 1st wire.
wires.r4c: 4 wires: exactly 1 blue → cut the 1st wire.
wires.r4d: 4 wires: more than 1 yellow → cut the last (4th) wire.
wires.r5a: 5 wires: last black + odd serial → cut the 4th wire.
wires.r5b: 5 wires: exactly 1 red + >1 yellow → cut the 1st wire.
wires.r5c: 5 wires: no black wires → cut the 2nd wire.
wires.r6a: 6 wires: no yellow + odd serial → cut the 3rd wire.
wires.r6b: 6 wires: exactly 1 yellow + >1 white → cut the 4th wire.
wires.r6c: 6 wires: no red wires → cut the last (6th) wire.
wires.blockedDesc: Without it the result is unknown — can't tell which wire to cut.
wires.blockedReason: With these wires ({n}) the first rule depends on whether the last serial digit is odd. Fill in above or in the left panel.
wires.notEnough: Click colors — result appears from 3 wires (now: {n}).
wires.note: The result recalculates with every click (3 vs 4 vs 5 vs 6 wires = different rules). Changing serial parity in the left panel also updates the result.

venn.title: Complicated Wires (VENN)
venn.help: For each wire set the LED, the color and the star from top to bottom. ✅ = cut, ❌ = leave, ❔ = enter the missing fact above.
venn.blockedDesc: Without it the result is unknown — {n} {word} {tail}
venn.blockedNote: Fill in via the banner above or the left panel — other wires compute normally.

button.title: The Button
button.help: Click the button color and the label from the bomb. The program walks rules 1–7 and says TAP or HOLD. On HOLD, pick the strip color after holding to get the release digit.
button.reason3: white button — rule 3 checks lit CAR
button.reason4: rule 4 checks > 2 batteries and lit FRK
button.needSelection: Pick a color and a label above — the result appears on its own.
button.blockedDesc: Without it the result is unknown — TAP or HOLD unclear.
button.blockedRule: Rule {n}: {r}. Fill in via the banner above or the left panel.
button.stripPrompt: After holding, a strip lights up — click its color:

memory.title: Memory
memory.help: Per stage: click the display digit (1-4), then for each position 1-4 click the label seen on the bomb. The program computes which button to press per the manual and remembers history (a wrong press on the bomb resets the module to stage 1 — then click Reset here too).
memory.labelsPrompt: 2) Labels on the 4 buttons left to right (click a digit under each position):
memory.needLabels: (fill in labels to point at a position)
memory.needHistory: Fill in earlier stages — this rule refers to history.
memory.resetHint: Click a row to edit a stage. A mistake on the bomb resets the module to stage 1 (click Reset here too).

maze.title: Maze
maze.help: All fixed circles are shown on the grid from the start (9 pairs). Hover a circle — the rest dim, only that pair stays lit. Click a circle to pick the maze, then click start (white square) and goal (red triangle). The program shows the shortest path (BFS).
maze.axesCaption: columns 1–6 left to right, rows 1–6 top to bottom • hover a circle to see its pair
maze.hoverNone: Hover any circle — only its fixed pair stays lit, the rest dim. Click to pick the maze.
maze.previewPair: Preview of pair {id}: {pts} — click a circle to pick.

knob.title: Needy Knob
knob.help: Needy module: the knob must be in the right position before its timer runs out. Click LEDs to copy the bomb. Positions are relative to the UP label, which may be rotated.
knob.ignoreNote: grey LEDs are ignored in this mode
knob.howLeft: left half matches the manual table
knob.howRight: right half matches the manual table
knob.noMatch: This combination matches no manual configuration — check the LEDs.

keypad.title: Keypad
keypad.help: Click the 4 symbols from the bomb. Non-matching symbols dim out; once the column is unique, the bottom shows the press order top to bottom.

whos.title: Who's on First
whos.thWords: Words (up to and including the key)

seq.title: Wire Sequence
seq.help: Click rows in order as red/blue/black wires appear (occurrences add up across panels). Highlighted rows show the cut rule for the last occurrence of each color.
